## Natural history notes

A small bluet damselfly characterized by its slender body, clear wings held together over the back, and blue-and-black patterning, with males showing bright blue markings along the thorax and abdomen. In Florida, it is found around ponds, lakes, marshes, canals, ditches, wet prairies, and other still or slow-moving freshwater habitats with emergent vegetation. Adults perch low on grasses, rushes, and stems while hunting tiny flying insects, and the aquatic nymphs live among submerged plants or debris where they feed on small aquatic invertebrates.
